    Evaluation Submodule

    SRToolkit.evaluation

    Classes and functions for evaluating symbolic regression approaches.

    Modules:

    Name Description
    parameter_estimator

    ParameterEstimator — fits free constants in expressions and ranks them by RMSE.
    sr_evaluator

    SR_evaluator — expression evaluation.
    model_store

    ModelStore — the SQLite storage behind an evaluator's models and trace, optionally a checkpoint file.
    results

    SR_results and ResultAugmenter — experiment results and the base class for their post-processing.
    result_augmentation

    ResultAugmenter implementations that post-process results with LaTeX, simplified forms, and held-out metrics.
    callbacks

    SR_callback and CallbackDispatcher — event-driven hooks for monitoring and early stopping during evaluation.

    EvalResult dataclass 

    EvalResult(all_models: list[ModelResult], trace: list[int], approach_name: str, success_threshold: float | None = None, top_k: int = 20, dataset_name: str | None = None, metadata: dict | None = None, wall_time: float | None = None, augmentations: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = dict(), default_constant: Constant | None = None, stop_reason: str | None = None, summary: RunSummary | None = None, checkpoint: dict[str, Any] | None = None, limits: list[dict[str, Any]] = list(), skips: dict[str, int] = dict())

    Result of a single SR experiment, as returned by SR_results[i].

    The stored data is the list of evaluated models and the evaluation trace; summary values such as min_error, best_expr, success and top_models() are derived from them. The ranking behind these summaries is cached. After construction models must not be modified or replaced, or the summaries can be stale.

    A result of a long run can instead keep only its top models and a RunSummary (keep_all_models=False, see SR_evaluator.get_results); its methods then give the same answers, except where noted. All models of such a run stay in its checkpoint, if it was kept (see open_checkpoint).

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    all_models list[ModelResult]

    All evaluated models, in the order they were first evaluated. trace indexes into this list. With a summary, only the top_k best models, best first.
    trace list[int]

    The evaluation trace. trace[k] is the index into all_models of the expression requested by the (k+1)-th counted call to evaluate_expr (a call that counts toward max_evaluations; see sr_evaluator). Cache hits appear as repeated indices; calls made after evaluation was stopped are not recorded. Every entry must be a valid, non-negative index into all_models; otherwise behaviour is undefined. Empty with a summary.
    approach_name str

    Name of the SR approach, or empty string if not provided.
    success_threshold float | None

    The experiment succeeds if an error strictly below this is found. A nan threshold is never reached. None if not set.
    top_k int

    Default number of models returned by top_models(). 0 means none; negative means all models.
    dataset_name str | None

    Name of the dataset. None if not provided.
    metadata dict | None

    The evaluator's metadata without dataset_name (e.g. model name, seed, and the dataset's metadata under "dataset_metadata"). None if there is none.
    wall_time float | None

    Seconds the run took, all sessions of a resumed run together (see SR_evaluator.wall_time). None if not known, e.g. from a checkpoint of a run that crashed before its first commit.
    augmentations dict[str, dict[str, Any]]

    Per-augmenter data keyed by augmenter name. Populated by ResultAugmenter subclasses via add_augmentation.
    default_constant Constant | None

    The default spec of the run (a Constant template): the spec of every parameter without one of its own (see ModelResult.free_constants). With it, resolve_constants (model.expr, model.free_constants, result.default_constant, symbol_library) gives the complete specs of a saved model. None for results saved in format 2.
    stop_reason str | None

    Why the run ended: "success_threshold", "max_evaluations", the reason of a callback (e.g. "time_limit") or of the approach (see stop), or "returned" if the search returned without stopping the evaluator. Any other reason than the first two marks a run that ended with budget left. None for results saved before it was recorded.
    summary RunSummary | None

    What is kept of the run instead of all its models, or None (default) if all_models and trace are complete.
    checkpoint dict[str, Any] | None

    A reference to the run's checkpoint, {"path": ..., "fingerprint": ...} (the absolute path and the evaluator's fingerprint, see Checkpoints), or None. SR_results.from_checkpoint, evaluate_approach and ExperimentJob.run set it when the file still exists as they return; get_results does not. Only open_checkpoint uses it.
    limits list[dict[str, Any]]

    The run's limit segments: one for its start and one per extension that changed something (a plain resume adds none; see Extending runs). Each is a dict with calls (the calls kept when the segment starts), max_evaluations (negative: no limit), success_threshold (None: none), callbacks (the to_dict() of each callback; [] if calls were made without callbacks, None if the segment made no call) and previous_stop_reason (why the segment before ended; None for the first, or after a crash). Check extended beside stop_reason before comparing runs. [] if not recorded (results saved before it was, or built by hand).
    skips dict[str, int]

    How many expressions the approach skipped without evaluating them, by reason (see count_skip), e.g. {"evaluated": 12, "rejected": 3}. Evaluated calls are not counted: calls that repeat an evaluated model (cache hits) number evaluation_calls - num_evaluated, rejected calls status_counts(per="call")["rejected"]. {} if the approach reported none, or if not recorded (results saved before it was, or built by hand).

    Examples:

    >>> models = [ModelResult(expr=["X_0"], error=0.5), ModelResult(expr=["C", "*", "X_0"], error=0.05)]
>>> result = EvalResult(
...     all_models=models,
...     trace=[0, 1, 0],
...     approach_name="MyApproach",
...     success_threshold=0.1,
... )
>>> result.best_expr, result.min_error, result.success
('C*X_0', 0.05, True)

    extended property 

    extended: bool

    Whether the run was extended with new limits: limits has more than one segment.

    An extension that changed nothing adds no segment, so it does not count. An extended run may differ from one that had its final limits from the start: e.g. an approach that reads its budget ran its first segment under the old one, and a time limit is not reproducible.

    num_evaluated property 

    num_evaluated: int

    Number of distinct models evaluated (an expression with its specs).

    len(all_models), or summary.num_evaluated. Includes models the trace never references.

    evaluation_calls property 

    evaluation_calls: int

    Number of counted calls to evaluate_expr, including cache hits (len(trace), or summary.evaluation_calls).

    min_error property 

    min_error: float

    Lowest finite error across all models.

    If no error is finite, the error of the top-ranked model (see top_models); this is +inf for results produced by the evaluator. NaN if no model was evaluated.

    best_expr property 

    best_expr: str

    Tokens of the best model joined without a separator (e.g. "C*X_0"). Empty if no expression was evaluated.

    success property 

    success: bool

    Whether min_error < success_threshold. False if no threshold is set or it is nan.

    top_models 

    top_models(k: int | None = None) -> list[ModelResult]

    Return the k best models, best first.

    Models with a finite error come first, sorted by error. Models whose error is not finite (inf or nan, not distinguished) come last. Only the error decides this, not the status; for results produced by the evaluator the two agree. Ties in error, and models that are all non-finite, are ordered by length (fewer tokens first), then by the order in which they were first evaluated. The returned objects are the ones in all_models, not copies.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    k int | None

    Number of models to return. Defaults to top_k. 0 returns []; a negative value or one larger than the number of models returns all of them (with a summary, the top_k kept ones).

    		 None

    Returns:

    Type Description
    list[ModelResult]

    The best k models, best first.

    Examples:

    >>> models = [ModelResult(expr=["X_0"], error=0.5), ModelResult(expr=["X_1"], error=0.1)]
>>> result = EvalResult(all_models=models, trace=[0, 1], approach_name="", top_k=1)
>>> [m.expr for m in result.top_models()]
[['X_1']]
>>> [m.expr for m in result.top_models(k=-1)]
[['X_1'], ['X_0']]

    def top_models(self, k: int | None = None) -> list[ModelResult]:
    """Return the ``k`` best models, best first.

    Models with a finite error come first, sorted by error. Models whose error is not finite
    (``inf`` or ``nan``, not distinguished) come last. Only the error decides this, not the
    status; for results produced by the evaluator the two agree. Ties in error, and models
    that are all non-finite, are ordered by length (fewer tokens first), then by the order in
    which they were first evaluated. The returned objects are the ones in ``all_models``, not
    copies.

    Args:
        k: Number of models to return. Defaults to ``top_k``. ``0`` returns ``[]``; a negative
            value or one larger than the number of models returns all of them (with a
            ``summary``, the ``top_k`` kept ones).

    Returns:
        The best ``k`` models, best first.

    Examples:
        >>> models = [ModelResult(expr=["X_0"], error=0.5), ModelResult(expr=["X_1"], error=0.1)]
        >>> result = EvalResult(all_models=models, trace=[0, 1], approach_name="", top_k=1)
        >>> [m.expr for m in result.top_models()]
        [['X_1']]
        >>> [m.expr for m in result.top_models(k=-1)]
        [['X_1'], ['X_0']]
    """
    if k is None:
        k = self.top_k
    ranking = self._ranking()
    if 0 <= k < len(ranking):
        ranking = ranking[:k]
    return [self.all_models[i] for i in ranking]

    def best_so_far(self) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
    """Return the incumbent history: each call in the trace where the best error strictly improved.

    Failed models (non-finite error) never become the incumbent. Only a strictly lower error
    changes the incumbent, so after a tie broken by length the last entry need not be
    ``top_models(1)[0]``. With a ``summary``, read from ``summary.incumbents``, which also
    holds each model.

    Returns:
        A list of ``(call_number, model_index)`` pairs, where ``call_number`` is 1-based and
        ``model_index`` indexes into ``all_models`` (with a ``summary``, into the full run's
        models, as in its checkpoint). Empty if no model was scored successfully.

    Examples:
        >>> failed = ModelResult(["X_1", "X_0"], float("inf"), status="invalid")
        >>> models = [ModelResult(["X_0"], 0.5), failed, ModelResult(["C"], 0.1)]
        >>> result = EvalResult(all_models=models, trace=[1, 0, 0, 2], approach_name="")
        >>> result.best_so_far()
        [(2, 0), (4, 2)]
    """
    return [(call, index) for call, index, _ in self._incumbents()]

    def calls_to_threshold(self, threshold: float | None = None) -> int | None:
    """Return the number of calls needed to first reach an error below ``threshold``.

    With a ``summary``, read from ``summary.incumbents`` (the same answer).

    Args:
        threshold: Error threshold. Defaults to ``success_threshold``.

    Returns:
        The 1-based call number at which an expression with a finite error strictly below
        ``threshold`` was first requested, or ``None`` if that never happened (always for a
        ``nan`` threshold). Failed models (non-finite error) never count. When aggregating
        over runs, treat
        ``None`` as censored at ``evaluation_calls`` rather than dropping the run (see
        [sr_evaluator][SRToolkit.evaluation.sr_evaluator]).

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``threshold`` is not given and ``success_threshold`` is ``None``.

    Examples:
        >>> models = [ModelResult(["X_0"], 0.5), ModelResult(["C"], 0.01)]
        >>> result = EvalResult(all_models=models, trace=[0, 0, 1], approach_name="", success_threshold=0.1)
        >>> result.calls_to_threshold()
        3
    """
    if threshold is None:
        threshold = self.success_threshold
    if threshold is None:
        raise ValueError("[EvalResult.calls_to_threshold] No threshold given and success_threshold is None.")
    # Errors strictly decrease along the incumbents, so the first one below the threshold is the first call.
    return next((call for call, _, error in self._incumbents() if error < threshold), None)

    def best_error_within(self, budgets: Sequence[int]) -> np.ndarray:
    """Return the best error found within each of the given numbers of counted calls.

    With a ``summary``, read from ``summary.incumbents`` (the same answer).

    A budget larger than ``evaluation_calls`` gets the run's final best error. This is exact
    for a run that reached ``success_threshold``, but only an upper bound for a run that
    stopped early for another reason (see [sr_evaluator][SRToolkit.evaluation.sr_evaluator]).
    Keep budgets at or below the experiment's ``max_evaluations``.

    Args:
        budgets: Numbers of calls, as ``int`` or numpy integers. Non-integers have undefined
            behaviour.

    Returns:
        Array of shape ``(len(budgets),)``, in the order of ``budgets``, with the best finite
        error within each budget.
        ``NaN`` where no model had been scored successfully yet, including every budget
        ``<= 0``.

    Examples:
        >>> failed = ModelResult(["X_0", "X_1"], float("inf"), status="invalid")
        >>> models = [failed, ModelResult(["X_1"], 0.5), ModelResult(["C"], 0.1)]
        >>> result = EvalResult(all_models=models, trace=[0, 1, 2], approach_name="")
        >>> result.best_error_within([1, 2, 3, 10])
        array([nan, 0.5, 0.1, 0.1])
    """
    incumbents = self._incumbents()
    calls = [call for call, _, _ in incumbents]
    curve = np.full(len(budgets), np.nan)
    for j, budget in enumerate(budgets):
        position = bisect.bisect_right(calls, budget)  # incumbents found within the budget
        if position > 0:
            curve[j] = incumbents[position - 1][2]
    return curve

    def status_counts(self, per: Literal["unique", "call"] = "unique") -> dict[str, int]:
    """Return the number of models with each [Status][SRToolkit.utils.types.Status].

    With a ``summary``, its stored counts.

    Args:
        per: ``"unique"`` counts each model (an expression with its specs) once; ``"call"`` counts every
            counted call in the trace, cache hits included.

    Returns:
        A dictionary with one entry per status in the order of
        [STATUSES][SRToolkit.utils.types.STATUSES], zeros included.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``per`` is not ``"unique"`` or ``"call"``.

    Examples:
        >>> models = [ModelResult(["X_0"], 0.5), ModelResult(["X_0", "X_1"], float("inf"), status="invalid")]
        >>> result = EvalResult(all_models=models, trace=[0, 1, 1], approach_name="")
        >>> result.status_counts()
        {'ok': 1, 'invalid': 1, 'rejected': 0, 'undefined': 0, 'error': 0}
        >>> result.status_counts(per="call")["invalid"]
        2
    """
    if per not in ("unique", "call"):
        raise ValueError(f"[EvalResult.status_counts] per must be 'unique' or 'call', got {per!r}.")
    if self.summary is not None:
        return dict(self.summary.status_counts if per == "unique" else self.summary.call_status_counts)
    models = self.all_models if per == "unique" else [self.all_models[i] for i in self.trace]
    counts = {status: 0 for status in STATUSES}
    for model in models:
        counts[model.status] += 1
    return counts

So errors strictly decrease along the front, and its last model is top_models(1)[0] whenever that has a finite error. With a summary, read from summary.pareto_front. The returned objects are the stored ones, not copies.

    def pareto_front(self) -> list[ModelResult]:
    """Return the models on the error-complexity Pareto front, shortest first.

    Complexity is the number of tokens (``len(model.expr)``). Failed models (non-finite error)
    are excluded. Of the models of each length, the one with the lowest error is taken (the
    first evaluated on ties); it is on the front if its error is strictly lower than that of
    every shorter model on it. So errors strictly decrease along the front, and its last model
    is ``top_models(1)[0]`` whenever that has a finite error. With a ``summary``, read from
    ``summary.pareto_front``. The returned objects are the stored ones, not copies.

    Returns:
        The models on the front, by increasing length. Empty if no model has a finite error.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the result has a ``summary`` without a front (written before fronts were
            recorded).

    Examples:
        >>> models = [ModelResult(["X_0"], 0.5), ModelResult(["X_1"], 0.7), ModelResult(["C", "*", "X_0"], 0.1)]
        >>> result = EvalResult(all_models=models, trace=[0, 1, 2], approach_name="")
        >>> ["".join(m.expr) for m in result.pareto_front()]
        ['X_0', 'C*X_0']
    """
    if self.summary is not None:
        if self.summary.pareto_front is None:
            raise ValueError("[EvalResult.pareto_front] The summary of this result has no Pareto front.")
        return list(self.summary.pareto_front)
    best: dict[int, ModelResult] = {}  # per length, the first model with the lowest finite error
    for model in self.all_models:
        length = len(model.expr)
        if math.isfinite(model.error) and (length not in best or model.error < best[length].error):
            best[length] = model
    front: list[ModelResult] = []
    for length in sorted(best):
        if not front or best[length].error < front[-1].error:
            front.append(best[length])
    return front

    def open_checkpoint(self, path: "str | os.PathLike | None" = None) -> "ModelStore":
    """Open the run's checkpoint read-only, to reach all its models.

    Its ``models`` and ``trace`` are read-only sequences that read from the file on demand, so
    a run of any length can be gone through without loading it (see
    [ModelStore][SRToolkit.evaluation.model_store.ModelStore]). Close it when done.

    Args:
        path: Where the checkpoint is now, if it was moved. Defaults to the path in
            ``checkpoint``. The fingerprint is checked either way.

    Returns:
        The checkpoint, opened with ``mode="read"``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``checkpoint`` is ``None``; if the file is a checkpoint of another run
            (its fingerprint differs from the one in ``checkpoint``; the message names the
            differing parts), which includes the run after an
            [extension][SRToolkit.dataset.sr_dataset.SR_dataset.extend_run] that changed its
            limits; if it is not a checkpoint, or one of another format version.
        FileNotFoundError: If no file exists at the path; the message gives the path.
    """
    # Imported here: model_store imports this module.
    from SRToolkit.evaluation.model_store import ModelStore

    if self.checkpoint is None:
        raise ValueError("[EvalResult.open_checkpoint] This result has no checkpoint reference.")
    target = self.checkpoint["path"] if path is None else path
    store = ModelStore(target, "read")
    try:
        saved = store.get_header("fingerprint", {})
    except BaseException:
        store.close()
        raise
    expected = self.checkpoint["fingerprint"]
    changed = sorted(k for k in saved.keys() | expected.keys() if saved.get(k) != expected.get(k))
    if changed:
        store.close()
        hint = (
            " If the run was extended, use the extended run's results."
            if set(changed) <= {"max_evaluations", "success_threshold"}
            else ""
        )
        raise ValueError(
            f"[EvalResult.open_checkpoint] The checkpoint at {os.fspath(target)!r} is of another run: "
            f"these parameters differ: {', '.join(changed)}.{hint}"
        )
    return store

    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
    """Return a JSON-safe dictionary of this evaluation result.

    The dictionary can be passed to ``json.dump``. After a JSON round trip,
    [from_dict][SRToolkit.utils.types.EvalResult.from_dict] restores every field exactly
    (including ``metadata``, ``augmentations`` and each model, see
    [ModelResult.to_dict][SRToolkit.utils.types.ModelResult.to_dict]), as guaranteed by
    [serialization][SRToolkit.utils.serialization]. The one exception is that numpy scalars come
    back as Python scalars.

    Returns:
        A dictionary with ``"format_version": 4`` and one entry per field
        (``default_constant`` as its ``to_dict``, ``summary`` as a dictionary of its fields
        with each model as its ``to_dict``, each ``None`` if not set). It also holds the
        derived summaries ``min_error``, ``best_expr``, ``success``, ``num_evaluated``,
        ``evaluation_calls`` and ``status_counts`` (per model), for reading the file
        directly (with a ``summary``, the counts are its own). ``from_dict`` ignores them.
        ``min_error`` is ``nan`` for a result without
        models, which ``json`` writes as the non-standard token ``NaN``.

    Raises:
        TypeError: If ``metadata``, ``augmentations``, ``limits`` or ``skips`` contain a value that cannot be saved,
            or a model's ``to_dict`` raises (see
            [ModelResult.to_dict][SRToolkit.utils.types.ModelResult.to_dict]). The
            message gives its full path, e.g. ``all_models[3].ranking_data['z']``.

    Examples:
        >>> result = EvalResult(all_models=[ModelResult(["X_0"], 0.05)], trace=[0, 0], approach_name="MyApproach")
        >>> d = result.to_dict()
        >>> d["trace"], d["min_error"]
        ([0, 0], 0.05)
    """
    summary = None
    if self.summary is not None:
        summary = {
            "num_evaluated": self.summary.num_evaluated,
            "evaluation_calls": self.summary.evaluation_calls,
            "incumbents": [
                [call, index, model._to_dict(f"summary.incumbents[{i}].")]
                for i, (call, index, model) in enumerate(self.summary.incumbents)
            ],
            "status_counts": dict(self.summary.status_counts),
            "call_status_counts": dict(self.summary.call_status_counts),
            "pareto_front": (
                None
                if self.summary.pareto_front is None
                else [m._to_dict(f"summary.pareto_front[{i}].") for i, m in enumerate(self.summary.pareto_front)]
            ),
        }
    return {
        "format_version": 4,
        "min_error": float(self.min_error),
        "best_expr": self.best_expr,
        "success": self.success,
        "num_evaluated": self.num_evaluated,
        "evaluation_calls": self.evaluation_calls,
        "status_counts": self.status_counts(),
        "approach_name": self.approach_name,
        "dataset_name": self.dataset_name,
        "success_threshold": None if self.success_threshold is None else float(self.success_threshold),
        "top_k": int(self.top_k),
        "metadata": _to_json_safe(self.metadata, "metadata"),
        "wall_time": None if self.wall_time is None else float(self.wall_time),
        "stop_reason": self.stop_reason,
        "augmentations": _to_json_safe(self.augmentations, "augmentations"),
        "trace": [int(i) for i in self.trace],
        "all_models": [m._to_dict(f"all_models[{i}].") for i, m in enumerate(self.all_models)],
        "default_constant": (
            None
            if self.default_constant is None
            else _to_json_safe(self.default_constant.to_dict(), "default_constant")
        ),
        "summary": summary,
        "checkpoint": _to_json_safe(self.checkpoint, "checkpoint"),
        "limits": _to_json_safe(self.limits, "limits"),
        "skips": _to_json_safe(self.skips, "skips"),
    }

    @classmethod
def from_dict(cls, data: dict) -> "EvalResult":
    """Reconstruct an [EvalResult][SRToolkit.utils.types.EvalResult] from the output of [to_dict][SRToolkit.utils.types.EvalResult.to_dict].

    Args:
        data: Dictionary produced by [to_dict][SRToolkit.utils.types.EvalResult.to_dict],
            possibly after a JSON round trip, of format 4, 3 (written before summaries and
            checkpoint references; ``summary`` and ``checkpoint`` load as ``None``) or 2
            (written before specs were recorded; ``default_constant`` and each model's
            ``free_constants`` load as ``None`` too). A missing ``stop_reason``, or a missing
            field of a saved ``summary`` that has a default, loads as ``None``; missing
            ``limits`` and ``skips`` load as ``[]`` and ``{}``. Unknown keys are
            ignored; other malformed input has undefined behaviour.

    Returns:
        The reconstructed [EvalResult][SRToolkit.utils.types.EvalResult].

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``format_version`` is missing (results saved before the evaluation trace
            was recorded) or not ``2``, ``3`` or ``4``, or if a model cannot be loaded (see
            [ModelResult.from_dict][SRToolkit.utils.types.ModelResult.from_dict]).
        ImportError: If the prior of a saved spec cannot be imported.

    Examples:
        >>> result = EvalResult(all_models=[ModelResult(["X_0"], 0.05)], trace=[0], approach_name="MyApproach")
        >>> EvalResult.from_dict(result.to_dict()).best_expr
        'X_0'
    """
    fmt = data.get("format_version")
    if fmt not in (2, 3, 4):
        if fmt is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "[EvalResult.from_dict] These results were saved by an older SRToolkit version, without "
                "an evaluation trace, and cannot be loaded. Rerun the experiment; with ExperimentGrid, "
                "delete the old result files first, since existing files count as completed jobs."
            )
        raise ValueError(f"[EvalResult.from_dict] Unsupported format_version: {fmt!r}. Expected 2, 3 or 4.")
    # Imported here: free_constants imports symbol_library, which imports this module.
    from .free_constants import Constant

    default = data.get("default_constant")
    summary = data.get("summary")
    if summary is not None:
        # A field with a default may be missing (saved before it existed): it loads as None.
        values = {
            f.name: summary.get(f.name) if f.default is not dataclasses.MISSING else summary[f.name]
            for f in dataclasses.fields(RunSummary)
        }
        values["incumbents"] = [(call, index, ModelResult.from_dict(m)) for call, index, m in values["incumbents"]]
        if values["pareto_front"] is not None:
            values["pareto_front"] = [ModelResult.from_dict(m) for m in values["pareto_front"]]
        summary = RunSummary(**values)
    return cls(
        all_models=[ModelResult.from_dict(m) for m in data["all_models"]],
        trace=list(data["trace"]),
        approach_name=data["approach_name"],
        success_threshold=data["success_threshold"],
        top_k=data["top_k"],
        dataset_name=data["dataset_name"],
        metadata=_from_json_safe(data["metadata"]),
        wall_time=data["wall_time"],
        augmentations=_from_json_safe(data["augmentations"]),
        default_constant=None if default is None else Constant.from_dict(_from_json_safe(default)),
        stop_reason=data.get("stop_reason"),
        summary=summary,
        checkpoint=_from_json_safe(data.get("checkpoint")),
        limits=_from_json_safe(data.get("limits", [])),
        skips=_from_json_safe(data.get("skips", {})),
    )

    ModelResult dataclass 

    ModelResult(expr: list[str], error: float, parameters: ndarray | None = None, ranking_data: dict[str, Any] = dict(), augmentations: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = dict(), status: Status = 'ok', status_detail: str | None = None, advisory_violations: list[CheckResult] = list(), free_constants: tuple[Constant, ...] | None = None)

    One evaluated expression: an entry of EvalResult.all_models.

    Two models are equal when their to_dict are equal.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    expr list[str]

    Token list representing the expression, e.g. ["C", "*", "X_0"].
    error float

    Numeric error under the ranking function (RMSE or BED). By convention +inf unless status is "ok"; this is not validated.
    parameters ndarray | None

    Fitted values, one per parameter in the order of parameter_labels, shape (n_parameters,), fixed values included; free_constants holds the specs they were fitted under. Set by the RMSE ranking only. None for other rankings and when nothing was fitted.
    ranking_data dict[str, Any]

    Freeform payload carried over from the RankingResult extra dict of the ranking function that scored this expression. Empty for rankings that emit nothing beyond score/parameters.
    augmentations dict[str, dict[str, Any]]

    Per-augmenter data keyed by augmenter name. Populated by ResultAugmenter subclasses via add_augmentation.
    status Status

    How the evaluation ended; see Status.
    status_detail str | None

    Why the status is not "ok": the parse error, the failed check of a required constraint (e.g. "MaxConstants: 9 constants, limit 8"), the exception, or the non-finite score. None for "ok".
    advisory_violations list[CheckResult]

    The failed checks of the evaluator's advisory constraints, as CheckResults with constraint and stage filled in; a check that raised is included, with error set. Pre-checks are recorded for every expression the evaluator could parse, whatever its status; post-checks only for models with status "ok". Pre-check results come first; within a stage, results follow the order of the constraints. Empty if no check failed, if the evaluator has no advisory constraints, or if the status is "invalid". It never affects error. See expression_constraints.
    free_constants tuple[Constant, ...] | None

    The specs parameters were fitted under (priors, bounds, fixed values), as Constants sorted by label; None when no specs were given. Parameters without a spec (bare C always), and a spec's unset prior or bounds, used EvalResult.default_constant.

    Examples:

    >>> result = ModelResult(expr=["C", "*", "X_0"], error=0.42)
>>> result.error, result.status
(0.42, 'ok')

    def add_augmentation(self, name: str, data: dict[str, Any], aug_type: str) -> None:
    """Attach augmentation data produced by a [ResultAugmenter][SRToolkit.evaluation.results.ResultAugmenter].

    A shallow copy of ``data`` is stored in [augmentations][SRToolkit.utils.types.ModelResult] with
    ``"_type"`` set to ``aug_type``. The caller's dict is not modified, but nested values are
    shared with it. If ``name`` is already taken, the first free key among ``name_1``,
    ``name_2``, … is used instead, so existing data is never overwritten.

    Args:
        name: Key under which the augmentation is stored.
        data: Augmentation data. Its values must be ones that can be saved (see
            [serialization][SRToolkit.utils.serialization]); otherwise
            [to_dict][SRToolkit.utils.types.ModelResult.to_dict] raises ``TypeError``. A
            ``"_type"`` key in it is replaced in the stored copy.
        aug_type: Augmenter class name, stored under ``"_type"``.

    Examples:
        >>> result = ModelResult(expr=["X_0"], error=0.1)
        >>> result.add_augmentation("latex", {"value": "$X_0$"}, "LaTeXAugmenter")
        >>> result.add_augmentation("latex", {"value": "$X_0$"}, "LaTeXAugmenter")
        >>> list(result.augmentations)
        ['latex', 'latex_1']
    """
    _add_augmentation(self.augmentations, name, data, aug_type)

    @classmethod
def from_dict(cls, data: dict) -> "ModelResult":
    """Reconstruct a [ModelResult][SRToolkit.utils.types.ModelResult] from the output of [to_dict][SRToolkit.utils.types.ModelResult.to_dict].

    Args:
        data: Dictionary produced by [to_dict][SRToolkit.utils.types.ModelResult.to_dict],
            possibly after a JSON round trip. Unknown keys are ignored; a missing
            ``advisory_violations`` (results saved before it was recorded) loads as an empty
            list, a missing ``free_constants`` as ``None``; other malformed input has undefined
            behaviour. Each saved
            [CheckResult][SRToolkit.utils.types.CheckResult] comes back equal, field by field
            (an ``inf`` amount included).

    Returns:
        The reconstructed [ModelResult][SRToolkit.utils.types.ModelResult].

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``data`` has no ``status`` (it was saved before statuses were recorded),
            or its ``status`` is not one of [STATUSES][SRToolkit.utils.types.STATUSES].
        ImportError: If the prior of a saved spec cannot be imported.

    Examples:
        >>> result = ModelResult(expr=["X_0", "+", "C"], error=0.25)
        >>> ModelResult.from_dict(result.to_dict()).expr
        ['X_0', '+', 'C']
    """
    if "status" not in data:
        raise ValueError(
            "[ModelResult.from_dict] This model was saved by an older SRToolkit version, without an "
            "evaluation status, and cannot be loaded. Rerun the experiment."
        )
    if data["status"] not in STATUSES:
        raise ValueError(f"[ModelResult.from_dict] Unknown status {data['status']!r}; expected one of {STATUSES}.")
    # Imported here: free_constants imports symbol_library, which imports this module.
    from .free_constants import Constant

    specs = data.get("free_constants")
    return cls(
        expr=data["expr"],
        error=data["error"],
        parameters=_from_json_safe(data["parameters"]),
        ranking_data=_from_json_safe(data["ranking_data"]),
        augmentations=_from_json_safe(data["augmentations"]),
        status=data["status"],
        status_detail=data["status_detail"],
        advisory_violations=[CheckResult(**r) for r in data.get("advisory_violations", [])],
        free_constants=None if specs is None else tuple(Constant.from_dict(c) for c in _from_json_safe(specs)),
    )

    def on_expr_evaluated(self, event: ExprEvaluated) -> str | None:
    """Dispatch to all callbacks and return the first stop reason.

    Returns:
        The reason of the first callback (in order) that asked to stop, ``"callback:<ClassName>"``

    def set_state(self, states: list[dict]) -> None:
    """Restore the states saved by an earlier dispatcher's ``get_state``.

    The state at each position goes to the callback at the same position if its import path
    (``callback_class``) is the same, and callbacks without a saved state are not called. A
    non-empty state (not ``{}``, which
    [get_state][SRToolkit.evaluation.callbacks.SR_callback.get_state] returns by default) whose
    class is only at other positions is dropped with a ``UserWarning``: the callbacks were
    reordered, so e.g. a time limit would start counting from zero. A state of a callback that
    is no longer there is dropped silently.

    Args:
        states: The saved states.
    """
    classes = [cb.to_dict()["callback_class"] for cb in self._callbacks]
    for i, saved in enumerate(states):
        if i < len(classes) and saved["callback_class"] == classes[i]:
            self._callbacks[i].set_state(saved["state"])
        elif saved["state"] and saved["callback_class"] in classes:
            warnings.warn(
                f"[CallbackDispatcher] The saved state of {saved['callback_class']} (position {i}) is "
                "dropped: that class is now at another position.",
                UserWarning,
            )

    EarlyStoppingCallback 

    EarlyStoppingCallback(threshold: float | None, max_evaluations: int | None = None)

    Bases: SR_callback

    Stops the search when the best error falls below a threshold or after a number of evaluations.

    The evaluator already enforces its own success_threshold and max_evaluations; use this callback for a tighter threshold or budget, or as an example of a stopping callback. Its stop reasons, "early_stopping:success_threshold" and "early_stopping:max_evaluations", differ from the evaluator's, so a run it stops counts as one that ended with budget left.

    Examples:

    >>> cb = EarlyStoppingCallback(threshold=1e-6)
>>> cb.on_best_expression(BestExpressionFound("", "X_0", 1e-7, 42))
'early_stopping:success_threshold'
>>> cb.on_best_expression(BestExpressionFound("", "X_0", 1e-5, 43))
True

    threshold: Error value below which the search is stopped. If None, each experiment's success_threshold is used. max_evaluations: Number of evaluations after which the search is stopped. If None, each experiment's max_evaluations is used (if it has one).

    def __init__(self, threshold: float | None, max_evaluations: int | None = None):
    """Args:
    threshold: Error value below which the search is stopped. If ``None``, each
        experiment's ``success_threshold`` is used.
    max_evaluations: Number of evaluations after which the search is stopped. If
        ``None``, each experiment's ``max_evaluations`` is used (if it has one).
    """
    self.threshold = threshold
    self.max_evaluations = max_evaluations
    # The limits of the current experiment: the given ones, or the experiment's where None.
    self._threshold = threshold
    self._max_evaluations = max_evaluations

    LoggingCallback 

    LoggingCallback(log_file: str | None = None)

    Bases: SR_callback

    Logs each new best expression to stdout or a file.

    log_file may contain placeholders that are resolved at experiment start using fields from ExperimentEvent. Available placeholders: {dataset_name},{approach_name}, {seed}. Using per-experiment placeholders (e.g. {seed}) gives each job its own file, which is the recommended approach for parallel execution.

    When multiple jobs share the same resolved file path, writes are protected by fcntl.flock (POSIX advisory locking) so concurrent processes on Linux / macOS do not corrupt each other's output. On Windows or network filesystems where flock is unavailable the lock is silently skipped.

    Examples:

    >>> cb = LoggingCallback()
>>> cb.on_best_expression(BestExpressionFound("Nguyen-1_ProGED_42", "X_0+C", 0.001, 10))
[Experiment Nguyen-1_ProGED_42] New best: X_0+C (error=1.000000e-03)
>>> cb = LoggingCallback(log_file="logs/{dataset_name}_{seed}.log")
>>> cb.on_experiment_start(ExperimentEvent(dataset_name="test", max_evaluations=10, seed=1,
...                                        success_threshold=0, approach_name="ta"))
>>> cb._resolved_log_file
'logs/test_1.log'

    def on_best_expression(self, event: BestExpressionFound) -> None:
    log_msg = f"[Experiment {event.experiment_id}] New best: {event.expression} (error={event.error:.6e})\n"
    if self._resolved_log_file is not None:
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(self._resolved_log_file)), exist_ok=True)
        with open(self._resolved_log_file, "a") as f:
            try:
                import fcntl

                fcntl.flock(f, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
                f.write(log_msg)
                fcntl.flock(f, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
            except (ImportError, OSError):
                f.write(log_msg)
    else:
        print(log_msg, end="")

    Raises:

            is not installed, or the config has no ``_bundle`` key and was never bound).
        TypeError: If ``callback_class`` is not an SR_callback subclass.
    """
    config = _auto_bind(config)
    target_cls = _import_class(config["callback_class"], "callback", SR_callback)
    return target_cls.from_dict(config)

    TimeLimitCallback 

    TimeLimitCallback(time_limit: float | timedelta)

    Bases: SR_callback

    Stops the search once a wall-clock time limit has elapsed.

    The timer starts when the experiment begins (on_experiment_start) and uses time.monotonic so it is unaffected by system clock adjustments. The stop request (reason "time_limit") is issued from the next expression evaluation after the limit is exceeded, so the search may run slightly past time_limit depending on how long a single evaluation takes.

    In a resumed run the limit spans all sessions: the time used up to the last snapshot is restored from the checkpoint. Time after that snapshot in a session that crashed is not counted.

    Examples:

    >>> cb = TimeLimitCallback(time_limit=60.0)
>>> cb.time_limit
60.0
>>> from datetime import timedelta
>>> TimeLimitCallback(time_limit=timedelta(minutes=2)).time_limit
120.0

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    time_limit float | timedelta

    Maximum wall-clock duration before the search is stopped at the next expression evaluation. Either a number of seconds or a datetime.timedelta, which is converted to seconds and stored as a float. Must be strictly positive.

    def __init__(self, time_limit: float | timedelta):
    """Args:
        time_limit: Maximum wall-clock duration before the search is stopped at the next
            expression evaluation. Either a number of seconds or a
            `datetime.timedelta`, which is converted to seconds and stored as a float.
            Must be strictly positive.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``time_limit`` is not strictly positive.
    """
    if isinstance(time_limit, timedelta):
        time_limit = time_limit.total_seconds()
    if time_limit <= 0:
        raise ValueError(f"time_limit must be strictly positive, got {time_limit}.")
    self.time_limit: float = time_limit
    self._start_time: float | None = None

    def set_state(self, state: dict) -> None:
    """Continue from the saved ``"elapsed"`` time; does nothing without it.

    Afterwards the elapsed time is the saved one plus the time since this call, whether or not
    ``on_experiment_start`` was called.

        self._start_time = time.monotonic() - state["elapsed"]

    def __init__(
    self,
    X: np.ndarray,
    y: np.ndarray,
    symbol_library: SymbolLibrary | None = None,
    seed: int | None = None,
    settings: Settings | None = None,
    default_constant: Constant | None = None,
) -> None:
    if symbol_library is None:
        symbol_library = SymbolLibrary.get_or_default()
    if settings is None:
        settings = Settings()
    if not isinstance(settings, Settings):
        raise TypeError(f"[ParameterEstimator] settings must be a Settings, got {type(settings).__name__}.")
    if default_constant is None:
        default_constant = uniform_default((-5, 5))
    if not isinstance(default_constant, Constant):
        raise TypeError(
            f"[ParameterEstimator] default_constant must be a Constant, got {type(default_constant).__name__}."
        )
    try:
        resolve_constants([], None, default_constant)  # raises ValueError unless it is a complete template
    except ValueError as e:
        raise ValueError(f"[ParameterEstimator] {e}") from None
    self.symbol_library = symbol_library
    self.X = X
    self.y = y
    self.seed = seed
    self.settings = settings
    self.default_constant = default_constant

    def estimate_parameters(
    self, expr: list[str] | Node, free_constants: Sequence[Constant] | None = None
) -> tuple[float, np.ndarray]:
    """Fit free constants in *expr* by minimizing RMSE against the target values.

    Expressions without free parameters (no constants, or only fixed ones) are evaluated directly,
    without running the optimizer. Limits on the number of constants or tokens are not checked
    here; [SR_evaluator][SRToolkit.evaluation.sr_evaluator.SR_evaluator] enforces them as
    required constraints.

    Args:
        expr: Expression as a token list in infix notation or a
            [Node][SRToolkit.utils.expression_tree.Node] tree.
        free_constants: Specs for labelled constants of ``expr`` (see
            [Constant][SRToolkit.utils.free_constants.Constant]); parameters without one use
            ``default_constant``. In any order; ``None`` or empty: all use it.

    Returns:
        A 2-tuple ``(rmse, parameters)``: the lowest finite RMSE evaluated and the parameters
        that gave it, one per parameter in the order of
        [parameter_labels][SRToolkit.utils.expression_tree.parameter_labels], fixed values
        included. If no evaluation was finite, ``rmse`` is ``nan`` or ``inf`` and the free
        entries of ``parameters`` are the optimizer's final point.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If a spec in ``free_constants`` has no label, two specs share a label, a
            label is not a labelled constant of ``expr``, or a spec that is not fixed has a
            ``value`` outside the bounds it takes from ``default_constant``.
        NotImplementedError: If ``initialization="mean"`` and a free parameter without a
            ``value`` has a prior that does not implement
            [ppf][SRToolkit.dataset.sampling.Sampler.ppf].

    Examples:
        >>> X = np.array([[1, 2], [8, 4], [5, 4], [7, 9]])
        >>> y = np.array([3, 0, 3, 11])
        >>> pe = ParameterEstimator(X, y)
        >>> rmse, constants = pe.estimate_parameters(["C", "*", "X_1", "-", "X_0"])
        >>> print(rmse < 1e-6)
        True
        >>> print(1.99 < constants[0] < 2.01)
        True
        >>> from SRToolkit.dataset import UniformSampling
        >>> from SRToolkit.utils.free_constants import Constant
        >>> spec = Constant(label="C_0", prior=UniformSampling(0, 10), bounds=(0, float("inf")))
        >>> rmse, constants = pe.estimate_parameters(["C_0", "*", "X_1", "-", "X_0"], [spec])
        >>> print(rmse < 1e-6, 1.99 < constants[0] < 2.01)
        True True
    """
    rmse, parameters, _ = self.estimate_parameters_with_info(expr, free_constants)
    return rmse, parameters

    def estimate_parameters_with_info(
    self, expr: list[str] | Node, free_constants: Sequence[Constant] | None = None
) -> tuple[float, np.ndarray, dict[str, Any]]:
    """Fit free constants in *expr* and report how the optimizer ended.

    Like [estimate_parameters][SRToolkit.evaluation.parameter_estimator.ParameterEstimator.estimate_parameters],
    and also reports how the optimizer ended.

    Args:
        expr: Expression as a token list in infix notation or a
            [Node][SRToolkit.utils.expression_tree.Node] tree.
        free_constants: Specs for labelled constants of ``expr``, as in ``estimate_parameters``.

    Returns:
        A 3-tuple ``(rmse, parameters, info)``. ``rmse`` and ``parameters`` are as in
        ``estimate_parameters``, so ``rmse`` is non-finite (``nan`` or ``inf``) if no
        evaluation was finite. ``info`` is empty when the optimizer did not run (no free
        constants, or only fixed ones). Otherwise it holds:

        - ``converged``: ``scipy``'s ``success`` flag;
        - ``evaluations``: RMSE computations (``nfev``), finite-difference gradient included;
        - ``iterations``: optimizer iterations (``nit``);
        - ``message``: the optimizer's message, only when ``converged`` is ``False``.

        ``converged=False`` does not mean a bad fit: RMSE has no gradient at a perfect fit, so
        L-BFGS-B often ends with ``"ABNORMAL"`` right at the optimum. Judge a fit by its error.

    Raises:
        ValueError: As for ``estimate_parameters``.
        NotImplementedError: As for ``estimate_parameters``.

    Examples:
        >>> X = np.array([[1, 2], [8, 4], [5, 4], [7, 9]])
        >>> y = np.array([3, 0, 3, 11])
        >>> pe = ParameterEstimator(X, y, seed=0)
        >>> rmse, constants, info = pe.estimate_parameters_with_info(["C", "*", "X_1", "-", "X_0"])
        >>> sorted(info)
        ['converged', 'evaluations', 'iterations']
        >>> info["converged"], info["evaluations"] >= info["iterations"]
        (True, True)
    """
    # Infix tokens: the specs are resolved against them, and they seed the random starting point.
    tokens = _as_tokens(expr, self.symbol_library)
    specs = resolve_constants(tokens, free_constants, self.default_constant, self.symbol_library)

    executable_error_fn = compile_expr_rmse(
        expr,
        self.symbol_library,
        backend=self.settings.evaluator.backend,
        X=self.X if len(specs) > 0 else None,
    )

    # The full parameter vector: fixed values in place, free entries filled in by the fit.
    parameters = np.array([s.value if s.fixed else np.nan for s in specs], dtype=np.float64)
    free = [i for i, s in enumerate(specs) if not s.fixed]
    if not free:
        return executable_error_fn(self.X, parameters, self.y), parameters, {}
    return self._optimize_parameters(
        executable_error_fn, specs, free, parameters, tokens, _spec_key(free_constants)
    )

    def __init__(
    self,
    symbol_library: SymbolLibrary,
    scope: str = "top",
    verbose: bool = False,
    name: str = "ExpressionSimplifier",
    rules: SimplificationRules | None = None,
    max_iterations: int | None = None,
    max_nodes: int | None = None,
    max_time: float | None = None,
    fold: Literal["none", "default", "keep"] | None = None,
    fold_aware: bool | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Simplified expressions of the best, top or all models of a result.

    Each expression is simplified by [simplify][SRToolkit.utils.expression_simplifier.simplify]
    with its model's ``free_constants``.

    Args:
        symbol_library: Symbol library of the expressions. It also decides which of the
            [DefaultRules][SRToolkit.utils.expression_simplifier.DefaultRules] apply.
        scope: Which expressions to simplify.

            - ``"best"``: only the best expression.
            - ``"top"``: the best expression and all top-k models.
            - ``"all"``: everything in ``"top"`` plus all evaluated expressions.
        verbose: If ``True``, emits a warning when simplification fails for an expression.
            Default ``False``.
        name: Key used in
            ``augmentations`` dict of [EvalResult][SRToolkit.utils.types.EvalResult] and
            [ModelResult][SRToolkit.utils.types.ModelResult].
            Default ``"ExpressionSimplifier"``.
        rules: As in [simplify][SRToolkit.utils.expression_simplifier.simplify].
        max_iterations: As in [simplify][SRToolkit.utils.expression_simplifier.simplify]; a
            non-negative ``int``, or ``None`` for its default.
        max_nodes: As in [simplify][SRToolkit.utils.expression_simplifier.simplify]; a
            non-negative ``int``, or ``None`` for its default.
        max_time: As in [simplify][SRToolkit.utils.expression_simplifier.simplify]; a positive
            number or ``None``.
        fold: As in [simplify][SRToolkit.utils.expression_simplifier.simplify], or ``None`` for
            its default (no folding).
        fold_aware: As in [simplify][SRToolkit.utils.expression_simplifier.simplify], or
            ``None`` for its default.

    Raises:
        TypeError: If ``rules`` is neither a
            [SimplificationRules][SRToolkit.utils.expression_simplifier.SimplificationRules] nor
            ``None``, or ``fold_aware`` is neither a ``bool`` nor ``None``.
        ValueError: If ``scope`` is not ``"best"``, ``"top"`` or ``"all"``; if
            ``max_iterations`` or ``max_nodes`` is not a non-negative ``int`` or numpy integer
            (``bool`` is rejected); if ``max_time`` is not ``None`` or a positive number
            (``bool`` and ``nan`` are rejected); if ``fold`` is neither ``None`` nor
            ``"none"``, ``"default"`` or ``"keep"``.
    """
    super().__init__(name)
    if scope not in ["best", "top", "all"]:
        raise ValueError(f"[ExpressionSimplifier] Invalid scope: {scope}. Must be one of 'best', 'top', 'all'.")
    _check_settings(rules, max_iterations, max_nodes, max_time, fold_aware)
    if fold is not None:
        _check_fold_mode(fold, "fold")
    self.symbol_library = symbol_library
    self.rules = DefaultRules() if rules is None else rules
    self.max_iterations = max_iterations
    self.max_nodes = max_nodes
    self.max_time = max_time
    self.fold = fold
    self.fold_aware = fold_aware
    self.scope = scope

    self.verbose = verbose

    def write_results(self, results: EvalResult) -> None:
    """Write simplified expressions into *results* and its models.

    Stores ``{"simplified_best_expr": ...}`` in the
    [EvalResult][SRToolkit.utils.types.EvalResult] ``augmentations``, and
    ``{"simplified_expr": ...}`` in each model's when ``scope`` is ``"top"`` or ``"all"``. A
    value is the simplified tokens joined into one string (e.g. ``"(C+C)*X_0"``). With folding
    (``fold`` other than ``None`` or ``"none"``), each entry also has ``"folded": True``: the
    simplified expression is then a different hypothesis. If
    simplifying an expression fails, its entry has no such key (with a warning if
    ``verbose``). A result without models gets an entry without ``"simplified_best_expr"``.

    Args:
        results: The [EvalResult][SRToolkit.utils.types.EvalResult] to augment.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``scope`` is ``"all"`` and *results* does not keep all its models (it
            has a [summary][SRToolkit.utils.types.EvalResult]); nothing is added then.
    """
    if self.scope == "all" and results.summary is not None:
        raise ValueError(
            f"[{type(self).__name__}] scope='all' needs all models, but this result keeps only its top models "
            "(keep_all_models=False)."
        )
    if not results.top_models(1):  # nothing was evaluated
        results.add_augmentation(self.name, {}, self._type)
        return
    best = results.top_models(1)[0]
    scoped = results.all_models if self.scope == "all" else results.top_models() if self.scope == "top" else []
    for model, key in [(best, "simplified_best_expr"), *((m, "simplified_expr") for m in scoped)]:
        data: dict[str, Any] = {}
        try:
            options: dict[str, Any] = {
                "max_iterations": self.max_iterations,
                "max_nodes": self.max_nodes,
                "fold": self.fold,
                "fold_aware": self.fold_aware,
            }
            simplified, _ = simplify(
                model.expr,
                self.symbol_library,
                model.free_constants,
                self.rules,
                max_time=self.max_time,
                **{k: v for k, v in options.items() if v is not None},
            )
            data[key] = "".join(cast(list[str], simplified))  # model.expr is a token list
            if self.fold not in (None, "none"):
                data["folded"] = True
        except Exception as e:
            if self.verbose:
                warnings.warn(f"Unable to simplify {''.join(model.expr)}: {e}")
        (results if key == "simplified_best_expr" else model).add_augmentation(self.name, data, self._type)

    @classmethod
def format_eval_result(cls, data: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    """Format experiment-level simplification data for display.

    Args:
        data: Augmentation dict containing ``"simplified_best_expr"``.

    Returns:
        A human-readable string, or empty string if no data is present.
    """
    simplified = data.get("simplified_best_expr", "")
    label = "Simplified (folded)" if data.get("folded") else "Simplified"
    return f"{label}: {simplified}" if simplified else ""

    def to_dict(self, base_path: str, name: str) -> dict:
    """Serialize the augmenter to a JSON-compatible dictionary.

        The augmenter.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``format_version`` is neither 1 nor 2.
        ImportError: If the class of the saved rules cannot be imported (see
            [SimplificationRules.from_dict][SRToolkit.utils.expression_simplifier.SimplificationRules.from_dict]).
    """
    if data.get("format_version", 1) not in (1, 2):
        raise ValueError(
            f"[ExpressionSimplifier.from_dict] Unsupported format_version: {data.get('format_version')!r}. "
            "Expected 1 or 2."
        )
    return ExpressionSimplifier(
        symbol_library=SymbolLibrary.from_dict(data["symbol_library"]),
        scope=data["scope"],
        verbose=data["verbose"],
        name=data["name"],
        rules=SimplificationRules.from_dict(data["rules"]) if "rules" in data else None,
        max_iterations=data.get("max_iterations"),
        max_nodes=data.get("max_nodes"),
        max_time=data.get("max_time"),
        fold=data.get("fold"),
        fold_aware=data.get("fold_aware"),
    )

    def __init__(
    self,
    symbol_library: SymbolLibrary,
    scope: str = "top",
    verbose: bool = False,
    name: str = "ExpressionToLatex",
) -> None:
    """Converts expressions inside the results to LaTeX strings.

    Args:
        symbol_library: Symbol library used to produce LaTeX templates for each token.
        scope: Which expressions to convert.

            - ``"best"``: only the best expression.
            - ``"top"``: the best expression and all top-k models.
            - ``"all"``: everything in ``"top"`` plus all evaluated expressions.
        verbose: If ``True``, emits a warning when LaTeX conversion fails for an expression.
            Default ``False``.
        name: Key used in
            ``augmentations`` dict of [EvalResult][SRToolkit.utils.types.EvalResult] and
            [ModelResult][SRToolkit.utils.types.ModelResult].
            Default ``"ExpressionToLatex"``.
    """
    super().__init__(name)
    self.symbol_library = symbol_library

    if scope not in ["best", "top", "all"]:
        raise Exception(f"[RMSE augmenter] Invalid scope: {scope}. Must be one of 'best', 'top', 'all'.")
    self.scope = scope

    self.verbose = verbose

    def write_results(self, results: EvalResult) -> None:
    """Write LaTeX representations into *results* and its models.

    Stores ``{"best_expr_latex": ...}`` in
    [EvalResult][SRToolkit.utils.types.EvalResult] ``augmentations``.
    Also stores ``{"expr_latex": ...}`` in each model's augmentations when
    ``scope`` is ``"top"`` or ``"all"``.

    Args:
        results: The [EvalResult][SRToolkit.utils.types.EvalResult] to augment.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``scope`` is ``"all"`` and *results* does not keep all its models (it
            has a [summary][SRToolkit.utils.types.EvalResult]); nothing is added then.
    """
    if self.scope == "all" and results.summary is not None:
        raise ValueError(
            f"[{type(self).__name__}] scope='all' needs all models, but this result keeps only its top models "
            "(keep_all_models=False)."
        )
    eval_data: dict[str, Any] = {}
    try:
        eval_data["best_expr_latex"] = tokens_to_tree(results.top_models(1)[0].expr, self.symbol_library).to_latex(
            self.symbol_library
        )
    except Exception as e:
        if self.verbose:
            warnings.warn(f"Unable to convert best expression to LaTeX: {e}")
    results.add_augmentation(self.name, eval_data, self._type)

    scoped = results.all_models if self.scope == "all" else results.top_models() if self.scope == "top" else []
    for model in scoped:
        try:
            model.add_augmentation(
                self.name,
                {"expr_latex": tokens_to_tree(model.expr, self.symbol_library).to_latex(self.symbol_library)},
                self._type,
            )
        except Exception as e:
            if self.verbose:
                warnings.warn(f"Unable to convert expression {''.join(model.expr)} to LaTeX: {e}")

    HoldoutMetric 

    HoldoutMetric(data: DataSplit | tuple[ndarray, ...], metric: str | Callable[[Callable[[ndarray], ndarray], ndarray, ndarray], float] | RankingFunction = 'rmse', scope: str = 'top', ground_truth: list | Node | None = None, ground_truth_constants: Sequence[Constant] | None = None, background_knowledge: BackgroundKnowledge | None = None, settings: Settings | None = None, seed: int | None = 0, refit_constants: bool = False, name: str = 'HoldoutMetric')

    Bases: ResultAugmenter

    Scores a result's models on held-out data.

    Use it to measure how the expressions found by a search perform on data the search never saw. Apply it with SR_results.augment; it adds the score of the best model to the EvalResult and, depending on scope, to each model.

    The kind of score depends on metric:

    • A built-in metric name or a callable ("rmse", "r2", "nrmse", "mae", "mse", or metric(predict, X, y) -> float): each model is evaluated on the held-out X with the constants fitted during the search, and compared with the held-out y. This measures how well the fitted model generalizes. Models without fitted constants (e.g. from a BED search) have them fitted on the held-out data first. With refit_constants=True, every model's constants are fitted on the held-out data, which measures how well the expression's form fits new data instead; these values are marked as refit. Requires y. Fits use each model's specs (ModelResult.free_constants).
    • A RankingFunction: the ranking is set up on the held-out data and scores each model, with its specs, e.g. BED on the held-out X.

    Scoring follows background_knowledge and settings, not the run's: in fits and ranking scores, constants without a spec, and a spec's unset prior or bounds, use the background knowledge's default_constant, not EvalResult.default_constant. To score under the search's task and settings, pass dataset.background_knowledge and dataset.settings.

    With every kind of metric, models the search could not score (any status other than "ok", e.g. rejected by a required constraint) get NaN; they are not scored on the held-out data.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    data DataSplit | tuple[ndarray, ...]

    The held-out data: a DataSplit (e.g. dataset.test) or an (X[, y]) tuple.

    		 required
    metric str | Callable[[Callable[[ndarray], ndarray], ndarray, ndarray], float] | RankingFunction

    A built-in metric name, a callable, or a RankingFunction (see above). Built-in names and callables are computed against the held-out y, so data must include it. Measures that need only the expression (e.g. complexity) belong in a RankingFunction or a separate augmenter. Default "rmse".

    		 'rmse'
    scope str

    Which models to score: "best", "top" (the result's top models), or "all". Default "top".

    		 'top'
    ground_truth list | Node | None

    Ground-truth expression passed to a RankingFunction metric's setup (e.g. for BED). Unused otherwise.

    		 None
    ground_truth_constants Sequence[Constant] | None

    Specs for the labelled constants of ground_truth, passed to a RankingFunction metric's setup. Unused otherwise.

    		 None
    background_knowledge BackgroundKnowledge | None

    The task. Expressions are compiled with its symbol_library and fitted with its default_constant; a RankingFunction metric's setup gets all of it (e.g. BED's samplers). None: a BackgroundKnowledge with only the active symbol library.

    		 None
    settings Settings | None

    Settings for fitting constants on the held-out data (estimation, evaluator.backend) and for a RankingFunction metric's setup. None: the defaults.

    		 None
    seed int | None

    Seed for the ranking setup (e.g. BED point sampling) and the constant fitting. The evaluator.ranking_seed setting overrides it for a ranking metric, but not for the refit of a string or callable metric. Default 0.

    		 0
    refit_constants bool

    Fit every model's constants on the held-out data instead of reusing those from the search. Only for built-in or callable metrics. Default False.

    		 False
    name str

    Key under which the values are stored in augmentations. Default "HoldoutMetric".

    		 'HoldoutMetric'

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ValueError

    If scope is invalid, if a built-in or callable metric is given held-out data without y, or if refit_constants=True is combined with a RankingFunction metric.
    TypeError

    If data is neither a DataSplit nor an (X[, y]) tuple, metric is not a string, callable, or RankingFunction, settings is not a Settings or background_knowledge is not a BackgroundKnowledge.

    Examples:

    >>> from SRToolkit.evaluation import SR_evaluator
>>> X = np.array([[1.0, 2.0], [8.0, 4.0], [5.0, 4.0], [7.0, 9.0]])
>>> se = SR_evaluator(X, 2 * X[:, 1] - X[:, 0], seed=42)
>>> _ = se.evaluate_expr(["C", "*", "X_1", "-", "X_0"])
>>> results = se.get_results(top_k=1)
>>> X_test = np.array([[2.0, 3.0], [4.0, 1.0], [0.0, 5.0]])
>>> results.augment(HoldoutMetric((X_test, 2 * X_test[:, 1] - X_test[:, 0]), metric="rmse"))
>>> bool(results[0].augmentations["HoldoutMetric"]["best_value"] < 1e-6)
True

    def __init__(
    self,
    data: "DataSplit | tuple[np.ndarray, ...]",
    metric: str
    | Callable[[Callable[[np.ndarray], np.ndarray], np.ndarray, np.ndarray], float]
    | RankingFunction = "rmse",
    scope: str = "top",
    ground_truth: list | Node | None = None,
    ground_truth_constants: Sequence[Constant] | None = None,
    background_knowledge: "BackgroundKnowledge | None" = None,
    settings: Settings | None = None,
    seed: int | None = 0,
    refit_constants: bool = False,
    name: str = "HoldoutMetric",
) -> None:
    """Scores a result's models on held-out data.

    Use it to measure how the expressions found by a search perform on data the search never
    saw. Apply it with [SR_results.augment][SRToolkit.evaluation.results.SR_results.augment];
    it adds the score of the best model to the
    [EvalResult][SRToolkit.utils.types.EvalResult] and, depending on ``scope``, to each model.

    The kind of score depends on ``metric``:

    - **A built-in metric name or a callable** (``"rmse"``, ``"r2"``, ``"nrmse"``, ``"mae"``,
      ``"mse"``, or ``metric(predict, X, y) -> float``): each model is evaluated on the
      held-out ``X`` with the constants fitted during the search, and compared with the
      held-out ``y``. This measures how well the fitted model generalizes. Models without
      fitted constants (e.g. from a BED search) have them fitted on the held-out data first.
      With ``refit_constants=True``, every model's constants are fitted on the held-out data,
      which measures how well the expression's form fits new data instead; these values are
      marked as refit. Requires ``y``. Fits use each model's specs
      (``ModelResult.free_constants``).
    - **A [RankingFunction][SRToolkit.evaluation.ranking.RankingFunction]**: the ranking is
      set up on the held-out data and scores each model, with its specs, e.g. BED on the held-out
      ``X``.

    Scoring follows ``background_knowledge`` and ``settings``, not the run's: in fits and
    ranking scores, constants without a spec, and a spec's unset ``prior`` or ``bounds``, use
    the background knowledge's ``default_constant``, not
    [EvalResult.default_constant][SRToolkit.utils.types.EvalResult]. To score under the
    search's task and settings, pass ``dataset.background_knowledge`` and
    ``dataset.settings``.

    With every kind of metric, models the search could not score (any
    [status][SRToolkit.utils.types.Status] other than ``"ok"``, e.g. rejected by a required
    constraint) get ``NaN``; they are not scored on the held-out data.

    Args:
        data: The held-out data: a [DataSplit][SRToolkit.dataset.data_split.DataSplit]
            (e.g. ``dataset.test``) or an ``(X[, y])`` tuple.
        metric: A built-in metric name, a callable, or a ``RankingFunction`` (see above).
            Built-in names and callables are computed against the held-out ``y``, so ``data``
            must include it. Measures that need only the expression (e.g. complexity) belong in
            a ``RankingFunction`` or a separate augmenter. Default ``"rmse"``.
        scope: Which models to score: ``"best"``, ``"top"`` (the result's top models), or
            ``"all"``. Default ``"top"``.
        ground_truth: Ground-truth expression passed to a ``RankingFunction`` metric's setup
            (e.g. for BED). Unused otherwise.
        ground_truth_constants: Specs for the labelled constants of ``ground_truth``, passed
            to a ``RankingFunction`` metric's setup. Unused otherwise.
        background_knowledge: The task. Expressions are compiled with its ``symbol_library``
            and fitted with its ``default_constant``; a ``RankingFunction`` metric's setup gets
            all of it (e.g. BED's ``samplers``). ``None``: a
            [BackgroundKnowledge][SRToolkit.dataset.background_knowledge.BackgroundKnowledge]
            with only the active symbol library.
        settings: [Settings][SRToolkit.utils.settings.Settings] for fitting constants on the
            held-out data (``estimation``, ``evaluator.backend``) and for a
            ``RankingFunction`` metric's setup. ``None``: the defaults.
        seed: Seed for the ranking setup (e.g. BED point sampling) and the constant fitting.
            The ``evaluator.ranking_seed`` setting overrides it for a ranking metric, but not
            for the refit of a string or callable metric. Default ``0``.
        refit_constants: Fit every model's constants on the held-out data instead of reusing
            those from the search. Only for built-in or callable metrics. Default ``False``.
        name: Key under which the values are stored in ``augmentations``. Default
            ``"HoldoutMetric"``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``scope`` is invalid, if a built-in or callable ``metric`` is given
            held-out data without ``y``, or if ``refit_constants=True`` is combined with a
            ``RankingFunction`` metric.
        TypeError: If ``data`` is neither a ``DataSplit`` nor an ``(X[, y])`` tuple,
            ``metric`` is not a string, callable, or ``RankingFunction``, ``settings`` is not a
            ``Settings`` or ``background_knowledge`` is not a ``BackgroundKnowledge``.

    Examples:
        >>> from SRToolkit.evaluation import SR_evaluator
        >>> X = np.array([[1.0, 2.0], [8.0, 4.0], [5.0, 4.0], [7.0, 9.0]])
        >>> se = SR_evaluator(X, 2 * X[:, 1] - X[:, 0], seed=42)
        >>> _ = se.evaluate_expr(["C", "*", "X_1", "-", "X_0"])
        >>> results = se.get_results(top_k=1)
        >>> X_test = np.array([[2.0, 3.0], [4.0, 1.0], [0.0, 5.0]])
        >>> results.augment(HoldoutMetric((X_test, 2 * X_test[:, 1] - X_test[:, 0]), metric="rmse"))
        >>> bool(results[0].augmentations["HoldoutMetric"]["best_value"] < 1e-6)
        True
    """
    super().__init__(name)

    if scope not in ["best", "top", "all"]:
        raise ValueError(f"[HoldoutMetric] Invalid scope: {scope}. Must be one of 'best', 'top', 'all'.")
    self.scope = scope
    # Imported here: SRToolkit.dataset imports this module.
    from SRToolkit.dataset.background_knowledge import BackgroundKnowledge

    if background_knowledge is None:
        background_knowledge = BackgroundKnowledge(SymbolLibrary.get_or_default())
    if not isinstance(background_knowledge, BackgroundKnowledge):
        raise TypeError(
            "[HoldoutMetric] background_knowledge must be a BackgroundKnowledge, got "
            f"{type(background_knowledge).__name__}."
        )
    if settings is None:
        settings = Settings()
    if not isinstance(settings, Settings):
        raise TypeError(f"[HoldoutMetric] settings must be a Settings, got {type(settings).__name__}.")
    self.background_knowledge = background_knowledge
    self.symbol_library = background_knowledge.symbol_library
    self.settings = settings
    self.metric = metric
    self.seed = seed
    self.refit_constants = refit_constants
    self._estimator: ParameterEstimator | None = None

    if isinstance(data, tuple):
        self._X = data[0]
        self._y = data[1] if len(data) > 1 else None
    elif hasattr(data, "arrays"):  # DataSplit (duck-typed to avoid an import cycle)
        self._X, self._y = data.X, data.y
    else:
        raise TypeError(
            f"[HoldoutMetric] data must be a DataSplit or an (X[, y]) tuple, got {type(data).__name__}."
        )

    if isinstance(metric, RankingFunction):
        if refit_constants:
            raise ValueError(
                "[HoldoutMetric] refit_constants applies to string/callable metrics only; a "
                "RankingFunction metric is set up on the data provided and refits constants there "
                "if it uses any (e.g. RMSE); it never uses the constants from the search."
            )
        self._ranking_mode = True
        self._metric_label = metric.name
        # Deep-copy so setup() mutates our own instance, not the caller's (which may be shared
        # with an SR_evaluator or another HoldoutMetric).
        self.metric = copy.deepcopy(metric)
        # As in SR_evaluator, a ranking_seed replaces the seed for the ranking.
        ranking_seed = self.settings.evaluator.ranking_seed
        self.metric.setup(
            self._X,
            self._y,
            ground_truth,
            ground_truth_constants,
            background_knowledge,
            seed if ranking_seed is None else ranking_seed,
            self.settings,
        )
    elif isinstance(metric, str):
        self._ranking_mode = False
        self._metric_label = metric
    elif callable(metric):
        self._ranking_mode = False
        self._metric_label = getattr(metric, "__name__", "custom")
    else:
        raise TypeError(
            f"[HoldoutMetric] metric must be a string, a callable, or a RankingFunction, got {type(metric).__name__}."
        )

    # A string/callable metric is computed against held-out targets, and missing model
    # parameters are refit against them too — both need y. Fail fast rather than silently
    # producing NaN for every model.
    if not self._ranking_mode and self._y is None:
        raise ValueError(
            f"[HoldoutMetric] metric {self._metric_label!r} requires held-out targets y, but the "
            "data provided none (a single-element (X,) tuple or a DataSplit without a 'y' array)."
        )

    def write_results(self, results: EvalResult) -> None:
    """Write the held-out metric into *results* and its models.

    Stores ``{"best_value", "metric", "refit_constants"}`` on the
    [EvalResult][SRToolkit.utils.types.EvalResult] and ``{"value", "metric", "refit_constants"}``
    on each scoped model.

    Args:
        results: The [EvalResult][SRToolkit.utils.types.EvalResult] to augment.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``scope`` is ``"all"`` and *results* does not keep all its models (it
            has a [summary][SRToolkit.utils.types.EvalResult]); nothing is added then.
    """
    if self.scope == "all" and results.summary is not None:
        raise ValueError(
            f"[{type(self).__name__}] scope='all' needs all models, but this result keeps only its top models "
            "(keep_all_models=False)."
        )
    # The best model is also in the scoped models, so score each expression once: rescoring would
    # cost a fit each time and, with a refit, could give a different value.
    values: dict[tuple[tuple[str, ...], str], float] = {}

    def value(model: ModelResult) -> float:
        key = (tuple(model.expr), _spec_key(model.free_constants))
        if key not in values:
            values[key] = self._value(model)
        return values[key]

    best = results.top_models(1)[0]
    results.add_augmentation(
        self.name,
        {"best_value": value(best), "metric": self._metric_label, "refit_constants": self.refit_constants},
        self._type,
    )

    scoped = results.all_models if self.scope == "all" else results.top_models() if self.scope == "top" else []
    for model in scoped:
        model.add_augmentation(
            self.name,
            {"value": value(model), "metric": self._metric_label, "refit_constants": self.refit_constants},
            self._type,
        )

def format_eval_result(cls, data: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    """Format experiment-level holdout data for display.

    def to_dict(self, base_path: str, name: str) -> dict:
    """Serialize this augmenter and write its held-out arrays to ``base_path``.

    Supported only with a built-in (string) metric.

    Args:
        base_path: Directory to write the held-out ``.npz`` into.
        name: Identifier used for the data filename.

    Returns:
        A dictionary sufficient to recreate the augmenter via
        [from_dict][SRToolkit.evaluation.result_augmentation.HoldoutMetric.from_dict]. The
        settings are saved with [Settings.to_dict][SRToolkit.utils.settings.Settings.to_dict];
        of the background knowledge only ``symbol_library`` and ``default_constant`` are kept,
        the parts a built-in metric uses.

    Raises:
        NotImplementedError: If ``metric`` is a callable or a ``RankingFunction`` (not
            serialisable — reconstruct such augmenters manually).
        TypeError: If a field of a custom settings section cannot be saved.
    """
    if not isinstance(self.metric, str):
        raise NotImplementedError(
            "[HoldoutMetric.to_dict] Only a built-in (string) metric is serialisable; "
            "reconstruct callable/RankingFunction holdout metrics manually."
        )
    import os

    if not os.path.isdir(base_path):
        os.makedirs(base_path)
    # Absolute, so loading does not depend on the working directory at save time.
    data_path = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(base_path, f"{name}_holdout.npz"))
    np.savez(data_path, X=self._X, y=cast(np.ndarray, self._y))  # a string metric always has held-out y

    return {
        "format_version": 1,
        "type": "HoldoutMetric",
        "name": self.name,
        "scope": self.scope,
        "metric": self.metric,
        "data": data_path,
        "symbol_library": self.symbol_library.to_dict(),
        "seed": self.seed,
        "refit_constants": self.refit_constants,
        "settings": self.settings.to_dict(),
        "default_constant": cast(Constant, self.background_knowledge.default_constant).to_dict(),
    }

    @staticmethod
def from_dict(data: dict) -> "HoldoutMetric":
    """Recreate a ``HoldoutMetric`` from its saved form.

    Args:
        data: A dictionary produced by
            [to_dict][SRToolkit.evaluation.result_augmentation.HoldoutMetric.to_dict].

    Returns:
        The reconstructed augmenter.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``data["format_version"]`` is not ``1``.
    """
    if data.get("format_version", 1) != 1:
        raise ValueError(
            f"[HoldoutMetric.from_dict] Unsupported format_version: {data.get('format_version')!r}. Expected 1."
        )
    arrays = np.load(data["data"])
    # Imported here: SRToolkit.dataset imports this module.
    from SRToolkit.dataset.background_knowledge import BackgroundKnowledge

    background_knowledge = BackgroundKnowledge(
        SymbolLibrary.from_dict(data["symbol_library"]),
        default_constant=Constant.from_dict(data["default_constant"]),
    )
    return HoldoutMetric(
        (arrays["X"], arrays["y"]),
        metric=data["metric"],
        scope=data["scope"],
        background_knowledge=background_knowledge,
        settings=Settings.from_dict(data["settings"]),
        seed=data.get("seed", 0),
        refit_constants=data.get("refit_constants", False),
        name=data["name"],
    )
